study type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score analysis
cohort: The study included individuals in the United States from 2015 to 2020 who delivered a liveborn singleton, nonanomalous neonate at term with a low-risk breech presentation.
finding: Term vaginal breech delivery was associated with slightly higher odds of the composite adverse neonatal outcome compared with cesarean delivery, though the absolute risk remained low, while short-term maternal outcomes were better for individuals who underwent vaginal delivery (excluding perineal lacerations).
mod_finding: Vaginal breech delivery was associated with slightly higher odds of composite adverse neonatal outcome (7.2% vs 6.3%) and higher neonatal mortality (0.4% vs 0.1%) compared to cesarean delivery, but had better short-term maternal outcomes (0.3% vs 0.5% for adverse composite maternal outcome excluding perineal lacerations).
